title: TRACE: Textual Relevance Augmentation and Contextual Encoding for Multimodal Hate Detection

bias_targets.methodology: Qualitative evaluation of the model's ability to detect subtle racial stereotypes and slurs in multimodal memes by analyzing the generated visually grounded captions and caption scorer predictions.

Qualitative analysis of the model's performance on memes that mock individuals with physical or developmental disabilities, comparing how different language models interpret the intersection of the image and text.
Qualitative analysis evaluating whether the model correctly identifies memes implying gender stereotypes and violence against women as hateful content.
Quantitative evaluation of offensive language identification using the MultiOFF dataset, which focuses on offensive memes generated during the 2016 US Presidential elections.

Quantitative evaluation (measuring Accuracy, F1, Precision, and Recall) of the model's ability to differentiate hateful memes from benign confounders using the Facebook Hateful Memes (FHM) dataset, which covers attacks across multiple protected characteristics (race, religion, sex, etc.).
